native_metadata.title: A first-order obstruction to Habiro's rank interpolation
native_metadata.description:
The ordinary integral rank completion printed in Ohtsuki's Conjecture7.30 cannot interpolate the standard unified sl_n invariants of any integral homology sphere with nonzero Casson invariant. A representative in one finite interpolation quotient forces the first q minus1 coefficient to be affine in matrix size n. The classical coefficient formula n(n squared minus1) times the Casson invariant is cubic. For the orientation of the Poincare sphere obtained by minus1 surgery on the left-handed trefoil, sizes1,2,3 give0, minus6, minus24, whose second difference is minus12. This supplies a decisive negative answer to the literal displayed conjecture. It gives no existence criterion at Casson zero and proposes no corrected completion.

The coefficient formula, theta/Casson and free-energy mechanisms are credited to Le2000, Le-Murakami-Ohtsuki1998 and Garoufalidis-Le-Marino2008; the fixed-Lie unification and Taylor identification are credited to Habiro-Le2016. The ordinary coefficient ring, common type-A parameter q=v squared=exp(h), matrix-size convention and assigned size1 invariant are explicit. Enlarged modern knot-color Newton rings are distinguished from the printed homology-sphere interpolation. No claim of novelty, first priority, present openness or exhaustive absence of earlier resolutions is made. Two independent bounded primary-source priority audits retain inaccessible bodies, selected-reading and citation-coverage gaps. Ohtsuki's volume year2002 and actual publisher release1June2004 are distinguished.

The deposit contains a concise three-page research note and source-free verification archive with editable LaTeX, all33 original PR952 files unchanged, five independent mathematical/priority family reports, exact arithmetic checks and a separately scoped strict portable finite verification profile. Source-free means third-party source bodies, extracts, images, raw private corpus and credentials are excluded; authored code is included. The new finite stages were reproduced on macOS CPython3.14.6 under isolated normal and optimized execution. The original source-dependent Linux/bubblewrap whole-filesystem read-only replay was not reproduced on this host. Cited topology theorems remain mathematical inputs. Hashes and finite identities do not certify topology, historical priority or a hostile-host sandbox.

The immutable submitted PR declares1/5; historical native per-turn count and total were not authenticated, and this audit adds zero substantive author proof-search responses. Extensive AI tools assisted solving, source research, computation, writing and adversarial review. native_metadata.title: A fixed-area exceptional set for positive squared-pole sums
native_metadata.description:
A full affirmative mathematical deduction for Baernstein's question, Hayman–Lingham Problem 7.37 (2307037 / AMR-022-7037). For every finite sum g(z)=sum lambda_j/(z-z_j)^2 with positive weights summing to one and arbitrary, possibly repeated, complex poles, there is one compact exceptional set S(g) of exact planar area pi, independent of R, such that the ordinary finite integral over D_R outside S(g) is at most 2 pi log R + pi(log 2 + 1/e) for every real R greater than one. The leading coefficient 2 pi is sharp; no optimality is claimed for the additive constant.

The deduction combines the established Eremenko–Hamilton 1995 indicator-transform inequality and the Levine–Peres 2009 quadrature/smash-sum construction, with their earlier Astala, Sakai and partial-balayage antecedents credited. No new singular-integral theorem, quadrature construction or general balayage/operator mechanism is claimed. Related recent work by Yongxi Lin and André Guerra is credited. The ingredients were logically available by 2009; a new target-specific application is distinguished from an earlier recorded full solution.

The extensive bounded priority audit identified no verified pre-PR full-target answer but does not certify historical novelty, worldwide first discovery/publication or global openness. Leung preliminary reports titled On a fixed area problem were located in AMS Abstracts 11 (1990), p.181, and 13 (1992), p.440; their mathematical text was inaccessible and relevance remains unresolved. Other unavailable full/final bodies and exact inspection limits are documented. Git version dates do not certify historical public visibility or causal independence.

The source archive preserves twelve original PR artifacts, three distinct mathematical audits, three priority approaches, an independent check that the 2002 EH correction does not affect the imported indicator bound, and the focused Leung supplement. Three standard-library mathematical control programs run offline in ordinary and optimized modes with complete-output comparison and actual failure guards where supplied. A fourth independent target control is reproducible with an explicitly requested, hash-pinned primary-source download. Floating calculations are diagnostics, not validated numerical or formal proof certificates. The universal proof is contained in the note.

AI tools were used extensively in proof development, computation, adversarial verification, literature research and writing. This note and supporting materials are unrefereed; independent AI reviews are not external human peer review, journal acceptance or formal proof-assistant certification.
